metadata.description: 40-prompt model-selection pilot for Project 2. This is a feasibility/capability-gap pilot, NOT a statistically representative sample of the LMSYS dataset.
metadata.classification_method: Deterministic keyword heuristic with mandatory researcher review and replacement
metadata.selection_method: 40 prompts total (10 per category: Factual QA, Summarization, Reasoning/Math, Creative). Selected from LMSYS Chatbot Arena single-turn English conversations.
metadata.review_status: Researcher review completed. 18 initial prompts replaced with clean, objective category-aligned candidates.

categories.factual_qa: Questions with specific, verifiable factual answers: names, dates, definitions, places, quantities, or explanations of how specific things work. The correct answer is a concrete fact.
categories.summarization: Requests to summarize, explain, describe, or give an overview of a topic, concept, or provided text. The task is to condense or present information clearly.
categories.reasoning_math: Math problems, logic puzzles, word problems, analytical reasoning, calculations, proofs, or any task requiring multi-step logical deduction with a verifiable numerical or logical answer.
categories.creative: Creative writing, brainstorming, roleplay, stories, poems, fictional scenarios, opinion pieces, or open-ended tasks where quality is subjective and no single correct answer exists.

Explain this:
"Recent advances in deep learning have relied heavily on the use of large Transformers due to their ability to learn at scale. However, the core building block of Transformers, the attention operator, exhibits quadratic cost in sequence length, limiting the amount of context accessible. Existing subquadratic methods based on low-rank and sparse approximations need to be combined with dense attention layers to match Transformers, indicating a gap in capability. In this work, we propose Hyena, a subquadratic drop-in replacement for attention constructed by interleaving implicitly parametrized long convolutions and data-controlled gating. In recall and reasoning tasks on sequences of thousands to hundreds of thousands of tokens, Hyena improves accuracy by more than 50 points over operators relying on state-spaces and other implicit and explicit methods, matching attention-based models. We set a new state-of-the-art for dense-attention-free architectures on language modeling in standard datasets (WikiText103 and The Pile), reaching Transformer quality with a 20% reduction in training compute required at sequence length 2K. Hyena operators are twice as fast as highly optimized attention at sequence length 8K, and 100x faster at sequence length 64K."
